answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may post orders or claim rewards. A rotating beacon selects a small sample of interactions for audits; if linked accounts reuse credentials, coordinate fabricated trades, or fail to deliver, the protocol can slash their deposits and withhold payouts. The juniper market might accept a saffron shipment only after this check. Sybils remain possible, but multiplying them means tying up more capital and risking greater losses, making attacks costly rather than free.
